first.rationale: Verify the strongest directly relevant onboarding evidence and the competing pricing evidence before committing. A guarded onboarding simplification test addresses both declining completion and activation while limiting the risk of improving early activity without sustainable qualified revenue; pricing remains an unresolved alternative given competitor pressure.

mid.rationale: Run a standard onboarding simplification experiment because the verified record directly addresses the 4% completion decline and shows improved time-to-value plus a 3% lift in 30-day retention, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not pursue promotional pricing this cycle: despite an 18% qualified-revenue lift, the 12% retention decline indicates poor first-renewal durability. Track activation, qualified revenue, and retention rather than relying on completion alone.

final2.rationale: Do not react to the deeper competitor cut with broad discounting: the verified promotion produced short-term qualified-revenue growth but a 12% retention decline at renewal, conflicting with sustainable growth. Run only a small, targeted referral test among established customers, where referrals previously added qualified revenue without measurable retention harm, while continuing the committed onboarding work. Treat referral impact on price-sensitive SMB churn as uncertain and monitor qualified revenue, renewal risk, and retention closely.
